The app is built in `/tmp/dsb-eval/opus-5-5/D-3`. It runs with `npx @angular/cli@19 serve`, and logging in with `admin` / `admin` reaches the dashboard. The production build passes, but only after I raised the per-component style budget in `angular.json` to 8 kB warning / 16 kB error: the dashboard stylesheet is 5.1 kB and went over the default 4 kB.

**How I checked it:** I ran a scripted pass in headless Chrome at 1280×900 and looked at the screenshots next to the Figma frames. Everything below worked, with no console errors:
- **Login:** an empty submit shows both field errors; a correct login writes `isLoggedIn` and redirects; `/login` sends a logged-in user to the dashboard.
- **Dashboard:** the log viewer adds a line every 3 seconds, and the seven bars render in near-black (#111111).
- **Profile menu:** it opens leftward and stays on screen, and closes on an outside click.
- **Users:** details, edit (PUT), edit → delete with the selected member kept, delete (DELETE), backdrop-close on the delete dialog, invite with validation and POST, and sign-out.

**Setup fixes:**
- The lockfile I started with pulled in Angular 21 as peer dependencies, so I deleted it and `node_modules` and reinstalled on 19.2.
- I renamed the project to `dsb-demo` in `angular.json`.

**What the token resolver changed:**
- **Chart bars:** it refused "darkest foreground colour". When I asked again as "filled high-contrast emphasis surface" it returned `surface-emphasis` (#111111), which is what the bars use. The decisions layer has no pure black (the brief expected one to be needed), so this is the closest thing the system has, not true black.
- **Chart plot height:** it suggested `size-bar-md`, but only because the word "bar" matched; that token is the application bar's height. I didn't use it. The chart height and log-panel height are literals in named local properties, with a comment in `dashboard.component.css`.
- **Monospace font:** the token set has no font-family tokens at all. The log font and the global Inter family are both literals, commented where they're set.
- **Card radius and page background:** my first questions came back "ambiguous". Asked more precisely, they gave `radius-2xl` for cards and `surface-subtle` for the recessed page background.
- **Login card shadow:** "card elevation" resolved to `shadow-modal`, which I used. It is heavier than the Figma shadow.
- **Dashboard tiles:** I gave them a border and no shadow.
- No raw colours or tier 1/tier 3 variables appear in `src/`. The one-pixel screen-reader utility and the two responsive breakpoints are also literals, because there are no breakpoint tokens.

**Where it differs from Figma (the spec took priority where they conflict):**
- **Content:** I used the spec's text and data everywhere, not the Figma copy (for example the login heading, tile values, service names, and Mon–Sun on the chart).
- **Dashboard layout:** I added the Data Summary tile the spec asks for, so there are three rows: four metric tiles; Throughput and Service Health; Data Summary and System Logs. I kept Figma's "System Overview" heading and throughput Peak/Average figures. The login divider is left out because the spec lists exactly what goes on the card.
- **Navigation:** Figma's Overview / Metrics / Logs / Settings links would have been dead, so the nav is **Overview** (`/dashboard`) and **Team Members** (`/users`).
- **Header:** `dsb-header` has no place to put a profile control, so the Online tag and user menu are laid over its right edge, lined up with the header's content. Header and footer links go through the Angular router instead of reloading the page.
- **Footer:** it uses `dsb-footer` with the columns the spec asks for, so it is taller than Figma's single-line footer.
- **Small differences:** the user table uses Details (least emphasis), Edit, Delete as the spec says, rather than Figma's order. Dialogs are the library's medium width (540 px, Figma shows 560). Card corners are 10 px (Figma shows 12). The biggest text size available is 22 px, so metric values are 22 px instead of 26.

**Not checked:**
- I didn't test viewports narrower than 1280 px.
- An avatar that fails to load should fall back to initials (I check each image first), but I never saw it happen because all the avatar images loaded.
